solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Beginning of hue and cry over nonsense

indicators.note: in an across clue, over says the pieces before it are turned round to read right to left
the opening letter of the word hue is taken

parts.note: to sob is to cry

explanation.surface: A public outcry is dismissed as rubbish from the very start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the whole of H plus SOB, so HSOB is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosh is an old-fashioned British exclamation for rubbish or empty talk.

clue.text: Travel permit shown by fools aboard vessel heading north

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means reading the letters from the bottom up
the fools are put on board, inside the vessel

parts.note: a sub (submarine) is a vessel
saps are gullible fools

explanation.surface: A permit to travel is produced by some idiots on a boat sailing northwards.
explanation.walkthrough: A bus pass is the British card giving free or cheap bus travel, often to pensioners.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus pass is a document entitling its holder to ride buses, a kind of travel permit.

clue.text: Pen range: inside is made from plastic

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

indicators.note: the short word is placed within the word for range

parts.note: to range is to roam, wander freely
of can mean made from, as in a ring of gold

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a pen and a range of products are made of plastic.
explanation.definitionFit: Styrofoam is a trade name for expanded polystyrene, a lightweight plastic.

clue.text: Basic principles I agree to stop enjoyable alcoholic effect

parts.note: something enjoyable is fun

indicators.note: the agreement word plugs, or stops up, the gap in the alcoholic effect

parts.note: the DTs, delirium tremens, is the shaking brought on by alcohol withdrawal
amen is said to show agreement, so be it

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to give up the pleasant buzz of drink as a basic principle.
explanation.definitionFit: Fundaments are foundations or basic principles of a subject, a less common word for fundamentals.

clue.text: One group in 10 like sport upset

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read from the bottom

parts.note: as means like, in the same way
RU is short for rugby union

explanation.surface: Someone in a sports team is unhappy, upset.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' points to the answer at 10 across, SKY; a group of stars in the sky is a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursa, the bear, names the constellations Ursa Major and Ursa Minor, star groups in the night sky.

clue.text: Ruddy inconsiderate swimmer!

parts.note: dam is a mild euphemistic spelling of damn, and ruddy is a mild British oath of the same kind
selfish means inconsiderate of others

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry at a swimmer who has hogged the lane.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruddy is a mild British swear word, a softened bloody; the exclamation mark keeps up the outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Damselfish are small, brightly coloured tropical reef fish, so a swimmer in the sea.

clue.text: Margaret forced to preserve government's lead

indicators.note: the outer word keeps the letter safe inside it, as a jar preserves fruit

parts.note: made someone do it means forced them to

indicators.note: the leading, first letter of the word government is used

explanation.surface: Margaret, perhaps a prime minister, was compelled to keep the government in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Madge is a traditional pet form of the given name Margaret.

clue.text: Mention in article promoted African lake

indicators.note: in a down clue, promoted means moved up, so the letters read upwards
the word for mention sits inside the article

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
to say is to mention

explanation.surface: A newspaper article mentions an African lake that is being publicised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoted' turns the whole assembly upwards, not just one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Nyasa is the old name for Lake Malawi, one of the great lakes of east Africa.

clue.text: What's viewed, talked about, when on railway?

definitions.text: What's viewed, talked about, when on railway?

indicators.note: in a down clue, being on something means coming before it, on top
spoken out, the word for viewed turns into a word that sounds the same

parts.note: what's viewed has been seen

explanation.surface: Asks what passengers look at and chat about on a train journey.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: the view from a train window is the thing passengers look at and talk about.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenery is the landscape one looks at, especially through a train window.

clue.text: Miracle-worker's home from Arizona region, mostly in north

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the abbreviation for north

parts.note: NTH is a written abbreviation of north
AZ is the postal code for Arizona

indicators.note: most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: an area is a region

explanation.surface: Tracing a holy man's home from Arizona to a region far up north.
explanation.walkthrough: NTH is a less familiar abbreviation of north, used in place names such as Nth Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Nazareth was the boyhood town of Jesus, whom the Gospels credit with working miracles.

clue.text: Chase in this star's home would be perfunctory

definitions.text: Chase in this star's home would be perfunctory

parts.words: Chase in this star's home would be perfunctory
parts.note: chase, in the engraving sense of etch, put inside the word for a star's home gives a word meaning hasty and superficial

explanation.surface: A celebrity's house hunt would be a half-hearted affair.
explanation.walkthrough: The star's home is the answer; put ETCH (to chase metal is to engrave it) inside it and you get SKETCHY, which is perfunctory.
explanation.definitionFit: Stars shine in the heavens, so the night overhead is where a star lives.

clue.text: Some demand Emu's safety, backing basis for anonymity

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the letters read right to left
some of the letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: Campaigners call for protection of the emu, supporting it without revealing who they are.
explanation.walkthrough: The run EMANDEMUSSA is taken from 'demand Emu's safety' and 'backing' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Using a false name, a pseudonym, lets someone act without their identity being known.

clue.text: Silky yarn's no good start for knitting waterproof jacket

indicators.note: no good means the letter for good is dropped

parts.note: angora is a soft silky yarn from rabbit or goat hair

indicators.note: the first letter of the word knitting is used

explanation.surface: A knitter finds silky yarn useless for starting a waterproof coat.
explanation.definitionFit: An anorak is a hooded weatherproof jacket; in Britain it also means a nerdy enthusiast.

clue.text: Ale drinking very mature? Anything but water

indicators.note: the beer takes in, drinks, the abbreviation

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
to age is to mature

explanation.surface: A drinker of well-aged ale wants anything other than water.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the sense in which water is not counted: a beverage is any drink other than plain water.
explanation.definitionFit: A beverage is a drink, in common use any drink other than water.

clue.text: Unlikelihood of brooding music number in topless attire

indicators.note: the music and number go inside the trimmed attire
in a down clue the top is the first letter, so it is dropped

parts.note: dress is attire
emo is a moody, emotional style of rock music
ten is a number

explanation.surface: It seems unlikely a moody song would be performed in revealing clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' leaves RESS, which the music and number split.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote chance is a slim one, so remoteness is slightness of probability.

clue.text: Firm in ocean fleet, at first not catching anything

indicators.note: the word for firm goes inside the word for ocean

parts.note: sea is a synonym for ocean
toned muscles are firm

indicators.note: the first letter of fleet is used

explanation.surface: A company's ocean fleet at first lands no fish at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not catching anything' wants to be about fishing; it means hearing nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stone deaf is completely deaf, so cannot catch a single sound.

clue.text: Welsh port abounding in pubs?

definitions.meaning: A port town in south Wales, near Cardiff
read as bar plus the adjective ending, full of bars, as sandy is full of sand

explanation.surface: A Welsh harbour town known for its number of pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Barry is a coastal town with docks in the Vale of Glamorgan, Wales.

clue.text: Ex-PM's policies with Murdoch say, breaking British strike

indicators.note: the name breaks into the word for strike

parts.note: to lam is to hit hard
Iris Murdoch was a novelist; say marks her as an example of the name

explanation.surface: A former prime minister's policies, backed by Rupert Murdoch, crush a British strike.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Rupert Murdoch the press owner; the wordplay wants the novelist Iris Murdoch.
explanation.definitionFit: Blairism is the political approach of Tony Blair, UK prime minister 1997 to 2007.

clue.text: Exertion intended to lead to Heaven's opening?

definitions.text: Exertion intended to lead to Heaven's opening?

parts.words: Exertion intended to lead to Heaven's opening
parts.note: the heavens opening means a downpour, and this ritual performance is meant to bring one

explanation.surface: Sounds like a strenuous pious effort to win entry to paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heaven's opening' suggests the gates of paradise; it is the idiom for rain pouring down.
explanation.definitionFit: A ritual dance performed to summon rain, used in some traditional cultures during drought.

clue.text: Annoyance with hotel — I'm not impressed!

parts.note: in British slang, to have the hump is to be annoyed or sulky
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A disgruntled guest is irritated by a hotel and voices disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: Humph is a grunt of doubt or disdain, a sound expressing scepticism.

clue.text: Pressure raised stores as well as order to submit

indicators.note: the turned word holds the link inside it, as a shop stores goods
in a down clue, raised means read from the bottom up

parts.note: a push is pressure applied
and means as well as

explanation.surface: A demand to submit raised pressure on stores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns PUSH into HSUP, which holds AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Hands up is the command telling someone to raise their hands in surrender.

clue.text: Stores maintained by skeleton staff?

parts.note: a skeleton staff is a bare minimum crew, but here skeletons are what is stored, in bone repositories

explanation.surface: Shops run by a minimal workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: A skeleton staff is a minimal crew; here the skeletons are the stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossuaries are vaults or chests where the bones of the dead are kept.

clue.text: Cover the woman in the presence of the man

parts.note: she refers to a woman
at, as in at a meeting, means being present there
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A woman covers up in front of a man.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe is to put into a sheath or casing, to encase or cover.

clue.text: Is one distraught about back-to-front slip? Far from it!

indicators.note: the scrambled letters go round the turned word
distraught means in a state, so the letters are thrown into disorder
the word for slip is written backwards

parts.note: to err is to slip up

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone is upset about putting on a slip back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distraught' rearranges IS ONE into NOSIE, which goes round RRE, the reversed slip.
explanation.definitionFit: No sirree is an emphatic American denial, equal to certainly not.

clue.text: Pipe down to the back passage?

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet, telling someone to pipe down
aft means towards the rear of a ship

explanation.surface: A pipe running down to a passage at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pipe' tempts as the definition; pipe down is a phrase for be quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaft is a narrow vertical passage, as in a mine or lift.

clue.text: Currency regulation impounds Berezovsky's capital

indicators.note: the regulation word shuts the letter inside, as a pound holds strays

parts.note: a rule is a regulation

indicators.note: the capital, first letter, of Berezovsky

explanation.surface: A financial rule freezes a Russian oligarch's money.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Berezovsky was a Russian oligarch; 'capital' looks like money but means his first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruble (rouble) is the monetary unit of Russia.

clue.text: I must leave ancient priest, say, returning skivvy

indicators.note: the letter I is taken out of the priest

parts.note: druids were priests of the ancient Celts

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: Someone must quit serving an old priest, perhaps, and go back to menial work.
explanation.definitionFit: A skivvy is British slang for a lowly servant doing menial chores, as is a drudge.

clue.text: Tart's outer thigh hiding bottom

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom letter is the last, which is hidden away

parts.note: the flank is the side of the body between ribs and hip, by the outer thigh

explanation.surface: Suggests a woman's thigh concealing her rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart's' reads as possessive but is 'tart is'; 'hiding bottom' drops the last letter of FLANK.
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open pastry case with a filling, a kind of tart.

clue.text: Label vegetable eaten by less evolved insects

indicators.note: the pieces are swallowed inside the rearranged letters
evolved means changed in form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: a tag is a label
beet is a vegetable

explanation.surface: A labelled vegetable is consumed by primitive insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evolved' rearranges the letters into SLES, which wrap the label and vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Stag beetles are large beetles whose males have antler-like jaws.

clue.text: Egg collected by ornithologists

indicators.note: the letters are held within the word ornithologists, as eggs gathered by collectors

explanation.surface: Bird experts gathering an egg.
explanation.definitionFit: A nit is the egg of a louse.

clue.text: Note, G&S part may involve rattling this off

definitions.text: Note, G&S part may involve rattling this off

indicators.note: rattling off suggests jumbling words at speed, so these letters are shaken up

parts.note: G&S stands for Gilbert and Sullivan, writers of comic operas

explanation.surface: A performer remarks that a Gilbert and Sullivan role may need this fired off fast.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a Gilbert and Sullivan role often includes a quick-fire comic song.
explanation.definitionFit: A patter song is a comic number sung at breakneck speed, a speciality of Gilbert and Sullivan.

clue.text: Bound west finally, carried by backless military vehicle

indicators.note: the letter rides inside the trimmed vehicle
the back, final letter, is removed

parts.note: a jeep is a military vehicle

indicators.note: the last letter of west is taken

explanation.surface: Heading west in a damaged military vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' tempts as heading for; it is a leap. 'backless' trims JEEP to JEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeté is a ballet jump from one foot to the other, a leap.
